Every error shown to a Kestrel user carries a code of the form `KST-` followed by four digits. The first digit gives the area: 1 for sign-in, 2 for connectors, 3 for queries and dashboards, 4 for members and seats, 5 for delivery and embedding, 6 for billing.

### KST-6002 — Payment declined

**Monthly plans** are not refundable. When a monthly plan is cancelled, it remains active until the end of the month already paid.

**Annual plans** can be refunded in full if the request is made within 30 days of the purchase or renewal date. After 30 days, annual plans are not refundable.

Refund requests must be sent by the workspace Owner to billing@kestrel.example. Approved refunds are processed within 10 business days and returned to the original payment method.

Charges caused by a billing error on our side (for example a duplicate charge) are always refunded in full, whatever the plan and whatever the date.

Refund requests must be sent by the workspace Owner, either from **Settings → Plan → Request a refund** or by e-mail to billing@kestrel.example. Approved refunds are processed within 14 days and returned to the original payment method.

Charges caused by a billing error on our side (for example a duplicate charge) are always refunded in full, whatever the plan and whatever the date.

## 7. Failed payments

When a payment fails, the workspace Owner and the billing contact receive an e-mail straight away. We then retry the payment automatically 1 day, 3 days and 7 days after the first attempt.

Each retry uses the payment method on file at the time of the retry, so updating the card before the next retry is usually enough to solve the problem. No lat

a payment fails, we retry the card automatically 3 days and 7 days after the first attempt, and the workspace Owner receives an e-mail after each failed attempt.

If the payment still fails, the workspace has a grace period of 14 days from the first failed attempt. During the grace period everything keeps working. After the grace period, the workspace becomes read-only: members can view dashboards but cannot edit them, and datasets stop refreshing.

A read-only workspace returns to normal as soon as the outstanding amount is paid.

The Owner can cancel a paid plan from **Settings → Plan → Cancel plan**. Cancellation stops future charges. The workspace stays on its paid plan until the end of the period already paid, then moves to the Free plan. Content above the Free plan limits becomes re

If all retries fail, the workspace enters a grace period of 21 days from the first failed attempt, during which everything keeps working. A banner reminds Admins that payment is overdue.

After the grace period, the workspace becomes read-only: members can view dashboards but cannot edit them, scheduled reports are paused, and datasets stop refreshing.

If the amount is still unpaid 60 days after the first failed attempt, the workspace is suspended: nobody can sign in to it until the outstanding amount is paid. A suspended workspace is not deleted, and returns to normal as soon as the payment succeeds.

Switching from monthly to annual billing is possible at any time and takes effect immediately; the unused part of the current month is credited. Switching from annual to monthly billing takes effect at the next renewal.

## 3. Payment methods

We accept credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express). Business and Enterprise customers can also pay by bank transfer against an invoice, with payment due within 30 days of the invoice date.

The card on file can be updated by the workspace Owner from **Settings → Plan → Payment method**. We do not store full card numbers; they are held by our payment processor.

Admins can make two-factor authentication mandatory for every member from **Settings → Security**. Members who have not set it up are asked to do so at their next sign-in.

### 5.2 Single sign-on

On the Business and Enterprise plans, workspaces can use single sign-on with any SAML 2.0 identity provider. To set it up, an Admin opens **Settings → Security → Single sign-on**, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel. We recommend testing with one Admin account before choosing **Enforce for all members**. When single sign-on is enforced, passwords are disabled and two-factor a

bers**. When single sign-on is enforced, passwords are disabled and two-factor authentication is handled by your identity provider.

### 5.3 Regaining access to your account

If you no longer have your authenticator device, use one of your backup codes at the second-factor prompt, then set up two-factor authentication again from **Profile → Security**.

If you have neither your authenticator device nor any backup code, ask an Admin of your workspace to reset your second factor from **Settings → Members**. You will set it up again at your next sign-in.

Version 4.2 · Last updated: 12 August 2026 · Audience: customers and workspace administrators

## 1. What Kestrel does

Kestrel Analytics is a dashboard and business intelligence service for teams. You connect your data sources, build datasets on top of them, and turn those datasets into dashboards that refresh automatically. Dashboards can be shared with colleagues, sent as scheduled PDF reports, or embedded in your own web applications.

Everything in Kestrel lives inside a **workspace**. A workspace has members, connectors, datasets and dashboards. Most customers use one workspace per company; larger organisations sometimes create one workspace per department. Members of one workspace cannot see the content of another workspace, even inside the same

## 10. Exporting and deleting data

The Owner can export the whole workspace (dashboards, datasets definitions and settings) as a ZIP file from **Settings → Workspace → Export**. Data from your sources is not included: Kestrel stores only the cached results needed to display dashboards.

When the Owner deletes a workspace, it is first disabled for 30 days. During that period it can be restored by contacting support. After 30 days it is deleted permanently and cannot be recovered.

Internal document · Owner: Customer Support · Last reviewed: 2 September 2026

## How to use this runbook

Every error shown to a Kestrel user carries a code of the form `KST-` followed by four digits. The first digit gives the area: 1 for sign-in, 2 for connectors, 3 for queries and dashboards, 4 for members and seats, 5 for delivery and embedding, 6 for billing.

For each code, this runbook gives what the user sees, the usual cause, what support can do, and when to escalate. Always ask the customer for the workspace name, the exact code and the time it happened. If a code is not listed here, escalate it to the on-call engineer of the Platform team.

Escalations go to the team that owns the service involved. The owning team of each servi

ions do not use a seat. A seat is used only when the person accepts the invitation. If the workspace has no free seat at that moment, the invitation cannot be accepted until an Admin frees a seat or the Owner moves to a larger plan.

Members can be removed at any time. Their dashboards are not deleted: they are transferred to the Admin who removed them.

### 5.1 Password and two-factor authentication

Members sign in with their e-mail address and a password, unless the workspace uses single sign-on. We strongly recommend turning on two-factor authentication from **Profile → Security**. Kestrel supports authenticator apps that generate time-based six-digit codes. When you turn it on, Kestrel shows 10 backup codes. Each backup code works once. Store them somewhere safe and separate from your

s. Each backup code works once. Store them somewhere safe and separate from your authenticator device.

Admins can make two-factor authentication mandatory for every member from **Settings → Security**. Members who have not set it up are asked to do so at their next sign-in.

### 5.2 Single sign-on

On the Business and Enterprise plans, workspaces can use single sign-on with any SAML 2.0 identity provider. To set it up, an Admin opens **Settings → Security → Single sign-on**, downloads the Kestrel service provider metadata, registers Kestrel in the identity provider, and pastes the identity provider metadata URL back into Kestrel. # Kestrel Analytics — Product Guide

Version 4.2 · Last updated: 12 August 2026 · Audience: customers and workspace administrators

## 1. What Kestrel does

Kestrel Analytics is a dashboard and business intelligence service for teams. You connect your data sources, build datasets on top of them, and turn those datasets into dashboards that refresh automatically. Dashboards can be shared with colleagues, sent as scheduled PDF reports, or embedded in your own web applications.

Everything in Kestrel lives inside a **workspace**. A workspace has members, connectors, datasets and dashboards. Most customers use one workspace per company; larger organisations sometimes create one workspace per department. Members of one workspace cannot see the content of another workspace, even inside the same
